solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hint — it’s all in cruciverbalist’s head, cryptically (9)

indicators.note: read cryptically, the letters are hidden in a scrambled form, so ITS ALL IN C is rearranged
a word's head is its first letter

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as anagram fodder
first letter of cruciverbalist

annotation.surface: A crossword setter owning up that the hint lies entirely inside their own devious mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface seems to talk about the setter's thinking, but 'it's all in' is literal fodder: its letters plus C rearrange to the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, so a hint of something.

entries.clue: Drink second whiskey with difficulty (5)

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet
as in 'ill at ease' or 'can ill afford'

annotation.surface: Someone struggling to down a second whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With difficulty' looks like an adverb for the drinking, but it supplies ILL, as in 'we can ill afford it'.
annotation.definitionFit: To swill is to drink greedily, gulping it down.

entries.clue: Nasty lice present — time for fast solution to this? (6,9)

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the eleven letters rearranged
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

annotation.surface: Lice have turned up, and something needs to be done quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is not speed but going without food, which gives the season LENT. 'This' points back to the lice, so the definition leans on the whole clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A liquid insect repellent is a solution in the chemist's sense, and it is the answer to a lice problem.

entries.clue: Turning up stove initially, I spoil Italian dish(8)

indicators.note: turning something over reverses it, and in a down clue the letters then read upwards
take the first letter of each of 'up' and 'stove'

blocks.note: first letter of up
first letter of stove
used as it stands
to mar is to spoil
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

annotation.surface: A cook admitting that turning up the heat has ruined the Italian pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like a phrase about the oven dial, but 'initially' reaches back to 'up' as well as 'stove'. 'Italian dish' reads as one phrase; only 'dish' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is the Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

entries.clue: Bar’s opening amid clamour — youth’s drinking port (8)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
amid means in the middle of, so B goes inside ROAR
to drink something is to take it in, so LAD takes RBOAR inside

blocks.note: a youth is a lad
a clamour is a roar
first letter of Bar, placed inside ROAR to make RBOAR

annotation.surface: A noisy bar where a young man is drinking port.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink in the scene is the definition in another sense: port here is the left side of a ship, not the fortified wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old term for port, the left-hand side of a ship facing forward.

entries.clue: In bed, I’m rolling over after a minute (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing within another, so IM sits inside the bed
rolling over turns the thing upside down, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
the reversed piece comes after A

blocks.note: used as it stands
a cot is a small bed
taken as written, placed in COT to make CIMOT

annotation.surface: Someone lying in bed turning over, a minute after waking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as a unit of time but is the adjective (my-NEWT), meaning tiny.
annotation.definitionFit: Atomic, in the sense of on the scale of atoms, means extremely small.

entries.clue: I run fleeing wild animal and slip (5)

indicators.note: I and R flee the animal, so they are taken out

blocks.note: used as it stands, to be removed
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, to be removed
a giraffe is a wild animal; I and R are taken out of it

annotation.surface: Someone running from a wild beast and losing their footing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slip' reads as a fall in the chase, but it is the social kind: a blunder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: slip in the sense of a social blunder, not a fall.

entries.clue: One goes on airship, essentially(6)

blocks.note: someone who goes on and on talking
the gas-filled envelope that is the heart of an airship

annotation.surface: Someone climbing aboard an airship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goes on' looks like boarding, but it means talks at length.
annotation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a windbag; it is also the bag of lifting gas that makes an airship fly.

entries.clue: Wood finish is hard to get off? Remarkably easy in Pacific Islands (6,9)

indicators.note: IS and H get off the wood finish, so they are removed
the letters of EASY IN are arranged remarkably, in a new way

blocks.note: French polish is a glossy shellac finish for wood
IS as it stands plus H for hard, both removed to leave FRENCHPOL
the six letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A complaint that French polish is hard to remove, answered: remarkably easy.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark closes one sentence and the answer seems to begin a new one; in fact the wordplay runs straight through both.
annotation.definitionFit: French Polynesia is the French overseas territory made up of islands in the South Pacific, including Tahiti.

entries.clue: With little energy, really stiff, that’s all (9)

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy; 'little' marks the abbreviation
really = very
a stiff is slang for a corpse

annotation.surface: Someone flagging, very stiff, and calling it a day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' reads as aching muscles, but as a noun it is a dead body.
annotation.definitionFit: Everybody means all the people, as in 'that's all of them'.

entries.clue: Elected certain Republican, one offering different policies (7)

blocks.note: a party elected is in power
certain = sure
R is the abbreviation for Republican

annotation.surface: A newly elected Republican who, for once, offers different policies.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'policies' look like a manifesto; they are insurance policies.
annotation.definitionFit: An insurer sells policies, and offers several kinds of them.

entries.clue: Revolting smell of sweat around place (7)

indicators.note: turned around, BO is read backwards

blocks.note: BO is body odour
the scene of a crime is its place

annotation.surface: A disgusting sweaty smell hanging round a place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but wrapping gives the wrong order; here it means turned around.
annotation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or disgusting, so revolting.

entries.clue: Filmed Herbert holding onto Charlie, United substitute (5)

indicators.note: LOM holds C and U within it

blocks.note: Herbert Lom, the film actor best known as Dreyfus in the Pink Panther films
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

annotation.surface: A film star, Herbert, clinging to a Charlie who is standing in for United.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filmed Herbert' is the actor Herbert Lom, not a verb; 'United' reads as a football club but gives only U.
annotation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest standing in for another, a substitute.

entries.clue: Select few that govern oil supply beginning to get sore about resistance (9)

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so OIL is bent into a new order
the beginning of 'get' is G
'about' means surrounding, so ACHY wraps round R

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
first letter of get
sore = achy
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, placed in ACHY to make ARCHY

annotation.surface: A cartel controlling the oil supply starts to feel the strain of resistance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun about the oil trade; it is the adverb supply (SUP-lee), flexibly, as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is rule by a small group, and by extension that group itself.

entries.clue: Frequency with which tax is put on raw materials in growth industry? (8)

blocks.note: F is the symbol for frequency
ores are mined raw materials
to tax someone's patience is to try it

annotation.surface: An economist asking how often a levy is charged on the raw materials of a booming sector.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' reads as a levy but is the verb meaning to strain; 'with which ... is put on' just strings F, ORES and TRY together.
annotation.definitionFit: Forestry is literally an industry of growing things, trees; the question mark flags the pun on growth industry.

entries.clue: Play with one dog holding up a length of rope (9)

indicators.note: CUR holds the reversed A L inside it
in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, so A L becomes LA

blocks.note: play = fun
I is the Roman numeral one
a cur is a mongrel dog
A as it stands and L for length

annotation.surface: Playing with a dog that is holding up a length of rope in its mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A length of rope' looks like one object; the definition is only 'of rope', an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Funicular means relating to a rope or cable, hence the cable-hauled funicular railway.

entries.clue: Doing burps too regularly (2,2)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: the even letters: bUrPs ToO

annotation.surface: Someone who burps far too often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doing' needs a phrase, as in 'what are you up to?'
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being up to something means being engaged in it, usually mischief.

entries.clue: Going north, say, are Irish politicians suitably prepared? (6,2)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so EG becomes GE

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, which is what 'say' can mean
used as it stands
the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, of Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: Asking whether politicians heading to Northern Ireland are properly ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going north' suggests travel to Northern Ireland, but it only turns EG upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Geared up means ready and equipped for something.

entries.clue: Old soldier and reservists taking aim in dispute (8)

indicators.note: 'taking' means taking in, so the old soldier holds the aim inside

blocks.note: a vet is a veteran
an end is an aim, as in ends and means
the TA, Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve

annotation.surface: A veteran and the reserves locked in an argument over what the goal is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old soldier and reservists' reads as a pair side by side, but the aim is swallowed by the soldier first. The TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve.
annotation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long-running feud, a bitter dispute.

entries.clue: Scruff’s last to remove rubbish lying around (4)

indicators.note: the last letter of remove
EPAN is turned round to read backwards

blocks.note: last letter of remove
to rubbish something is to pan it

annotation.surface: A scruffy person who is last to clear away the rubbish lying about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scruff' looks like an untidy person, but it is the back of the neck, as in 'by the scruff of the neck'.
annotation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, which is the nape.

entries.clue: Communist tactic restricts European action once more (8)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the letters of RED PLOY close round E

blocks.note: a Red is a communist
a ploy is a tactic
E is the abbreviation for European, placed between RED and PLOY

annotation.surface: A communist manoeuvre that hems in European activity again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Action' is the office-speak verb, to put into action, so 'action once more' matches a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To redeploy is to put people or resources into action again, in a new role.

entries.clue: Something left behind in Faraday cage lights up (6)

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow
in a down clue, up means read upwards, so the hidden letters come out reversed

blocks.note: hidden in faradaY CAGE Lights

annotation.surface: Lights flashing up in a Faraday cage somebody left behind in the lab.
annotation.walkthrough: A Faraday cage is a metal enclosure that blocks electric fields. 'Lights up' reads as illuminating; 'up' is the reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A legacy is what someone leaves behind, whether money in a will or a lasting influence.

entries.clue: What has no part ultimately in outside broadcast (6)

definitions.text: What has no part ultimately in outside broadcast

indicators.note: no part means that part is removed
the ultimate part of 'outside' is its last letter, E
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so OUTSID is scattered into a new order

blocks.note: OUTSIDE with its last letter removed

annotation.surface: A riddle asking what place plays no role in a broadcast from outside.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the definition: an outside broadcast is one made away from the studio, so the studio has no part in it.
annotation.definitionFit: Outside broadcasts are, by definition, those not made in the studio.

entries.clue: I gather prayer book’s missing from Globe (9)

definitions.note: The definition is cryptic: a collector is someone who could say 'I gather'.

indicators.note: B is missing from ORB, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a collect is a short prayer in the Anglican and Catholic liturgy
B is the abbreviation for book, to be removed
an orb is a globe; without B it is OR

annotation.surface: Someone who has heard that the prayer book has gone missing from the Globe theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prayer book' reads as one object, but splits into prayer (COLLECT) and book (B). 'I gather' looks like 'I hear' but is the answer speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: A collector gathers things, so could describe themselves with 'I gather'.

entries.clue: US politician briefly tours northern India for material (5)

indicators.note: a brief form, the abbreviation DEM
to tour is to go round, so DEM goes round N and I

blocks.note: Dem is short for Democrat
N is the abbreviation for northern
I is India in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American politician on a quick tour of northern India, buying cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northern India' reads as a region, but it is two separate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Denim is the tough cotton cloth used for jeans.

entries.clue: It’s tucked inside Mr Ellington’s top hat (5)

indicators.note: 'it is tucked inside' means placed within, so IT goes between the other letters
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: used as it stands
used as it stands
first letter of Ellington

annotation.surface: Something tucked into Duke Ellington's top hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top hat' reads as one phrase, but 'top' belongs to Ellington and the definition is just 'hat'.
annotation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by bishops.

entries.clue: Repeated echoes, in a manner of speaking, returned downwind (7)

indicators.note: EE goes inside the reversed DRAWL
DRAWL is sent back, read backwards as LWARD

blocks.note: a drawl is a slow way of speaking
E is echo in the NATO alphabet, twice over

annotation.surface: Echoes coming back on the wind, repeated like a way of talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom meaning 'so to speak', but it is the container signal plus a drawl.
annotation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side away from the wind, so downwind.

entries.clue: Some arrived at a settlement to find a bunch of logs? (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used: the answer is part of the phrase

blocks.note: hidden in arriveD AT A SETtlement

annotation.surface: Settlers arriving at a frontier village to find a pile of cut logs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Logs' are wood in the surface, but in computing a log is a record of events, and a collection of them is data.
annotation.definitionFit: A dataset is a collection of data, such as a bunch of computer logs; the question mark flags the pun.

entries.clue: Fancy heading for Rome? Temperature variable in the case of Italy (5)

indicators.note: the heading of Rome is its first letter
T and Z go inside the case of Italy
a word's case is its outer letters, I and Y

blocks.note: first letter of Rome
outer letters of Italy
T is the symbol for temperature
algebra uses x, y and z for variables

annotation.surface: A tourist wondering whether to head for Rome, given that Italy's weather is so changeable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temperature variable' reads as changeable weather, but it is two letters, T and Z.
annotation.definitionFit: Ritzy means fancy and luxurious, after the Ritz hotels.

entries.clue: Children’s facility external to hospital is returning for an extended time (9)

indicators.note: ORP is placed outside H, on its front
PRO comes back, read backwards as ORP

blocks.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
used as it stands
an age is a very long time

annotation.surface: A children's unit just outside the hospital that keeps coming back for long stays.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' reads as a link, but it gives PRO; the same word could never be the link here because every other word is used.
annotation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution caring for children without parents.
